ATP Masters 1000 event to be held from 5-12 April April 04, 2026 Getty Images Carlos Alcaraz is the defending champion in Monte-Carlo. By ATP Staff The third ATP Masters 1000 event of the season and first on clay begins on Sunday at the Rolex Monte-Carlo Masters. Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner and Alexander Zverev are among the stars that will headline the tournament in the Principality. The event will be broadcast worldwide and you can view how to watch the tournament below. The 22-year-old Spaniard will face Stan Wawrinka or Sebastian Baez in his opener. Top Videos World No. 2 Jannik Sinner has the opportunity to climb to No. 1 in the PIF ATP Rankings this week. The Italian holds a 10-4 record at the tournament, according to the Infosys ATP Win/Loss Index, with his best result semi-final showings in 2023 and 2024. Sinner has won his past 12 matches after winning Indian Wells and Miami in March. Read more from Monte-Carlo Sinner & Alcaraz's Monte-Carlo draw: Which intriguing opponents could they face in R2? How Sinner can become World No. 1 in Monte-Carlo 2026 Monte-Carlo tennis prize money French stars Gael Monfils and Moise Kouame have received wild cards. Monfils, a finalist in 2016, is set for his final appearance at the event, while 17-year-old Kouame is making his debut. Kouame opens against Ugo Humbert and could play Sinner in the second round.
